Scientific Summary
This report provides a gene‑centric view of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) and virulence genes across 40 Pseudomonas aeruginosa genomes. Each gene is shown with the complete list of genomes that carry it. The dashboard summarises key typing results.

Population Structure Overview
Pseudomonas aeruginosa is an opportunistic pathogen with high intrinsic and acquired resistance. Understanding its population structure helps track outbreaks and resistance dissemination.
  • MLST (Sequence Type): Multi‑locus sequence typing (Pasteur scheme) defines STs. Dominant clones like ST111, ST235, ST244 are often associated with multidrug resistance.
  • O‑Serotype: Lipopolysaccharide O‑antigen types (e.g., O1–O20). Certain serotypes correlate with clinical syndromes and biofilm formation.
  • N50: Assembly quality metric (the shortest contig length such that half the genome is in contigs of that size or larger).

MLST (Pasteur scheme)
Multi‑locus sequence typing uses internal fragments of seven housekeeping genes (acsA, aroE, guaA, mutL, nuoD, ppsA, trpE). Each unique combination defines a Sequence Type (ST). Globally disseminated high‑risk clones include ST111, ST235, ST244, ST277, etc.

O‑Serotype (PAST)
The O‑antigen is a major surface determinant and vaccine target. P. aeruginosa has 20 serotypes (O1–O20). Certain serotypes are associated with chronic infections (e.g., O1, O2, O5, O6, O11) and high‑risk clones.

Antimicrobial Resistance Genes
Pseudomonas aeruginosa exhibits both intrinsic resistance (e.g., efflux pumps, AmpC) and acquired resistance (carbapenemases, ESBLs, 16S rRNA methyltransferases). Critical resistance genes include blaKPC, blaNDM, blaVIM, blaIMP, blaOXA‑48‑like, mcr (colistin), and armA/rmt (aminoglycosides). Use filter buttons to focus on major classes.

Virulence Factors
Pseudomonas aeruginosa produces numerous virulence factors including the type III secretion system (T3SS) effectors ExoU, ExoS, ExoT, ExoY, exotoxin A (ToxA), elastases (LasB, LasA), pyocyanin, alginate, and siderophores. The presence of exoU is associated with acute cytotoxicity and poor outcomes.
